evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx — all FOUR state-changing mutation handlers swallow their error with only a bare console.error and surface NOTHING to the user: handlePetDelete (:98-108, catch at :103-104 `console.error('Failed to delete pet registration:', error)`), handlePetReview / approve-reject (:111-125, catch at :120-121), handleVehicleDelete (:155-165, catch at :160-161), and handleVehicleReview (:168-182, catch at :177-178). Each does `await ...Mutation.mutateAsync(...)` inside try/catch and, on failure, only logs to the console.

The file imports nothing that could surface an error: `grep` for toast / useToast / setError / errorMessage / onError / .isError / import.meta.env.DEV over the file returns ZERO hits, and its import list (:8-12) is only @ppt/api-client + React hooks + the two list components — no Toast, no useTranslation, no error state. The child lists receive only registration data + pending/paging props (petListData/vehicleListData built at :189-215); no mutation-error prop is passed down (PetRegistrationList / VehicleRegistrationList). So when a manager clicks Delete or Approve/Reject on a pet or vehicle registration and the request fails (network drop, 403 from RLS, 409 conflict), the row simply stays as-is with no toast, banner, or inline message — the user believes the destructive/approval action succeeded when it silently did not. This is the same silent-mutation-failure class already filed for accounting (accounting-invoice-silent-fail) and facilities (facilities-booking-silent-errors), now confirmed on the registry management page, which was previously only reviewed for its navigation anti-pattern (registry-full-reload-nav, 2026-09-20) — distinct defect, not a duplicate.

The un-gated console.error also violates the app's DEV-gated-logging convention (ppt-web-core's logging is import.meta.env.DEV-guarded per the 2026-09-23 core review) — these five console.error calls ship to production consoles. Landable frontend-only remedy: surface each mutation failure to the user (Toast via the app's existing Toast/useToast, or an inline error state passed to the list), and DEV-gate or remove the raw console.error. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest/RTL test that makes mutateAsync reject and asserts an error toast/message is rendered. Confidence medium: the missing error surface is confirmed by static read + grep of the file and its children; production reachability of the failure branch is inferred, not runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx renders its entire UI with hardcoded English string literals and never imports react-i18next (no `useTranslation` / `t(...)` in the file; import list :8-12 has no i18n). Confirmed hardcoded user-facing strings: the page heading `Building Registries` (:220) and subtitle `Manage pet and vehicle registrations for your building` (:221), and the tab labels `Pets` / `Vehicles` (:239, and the vehicles tab below). The <title> SVG labels (`Pets`) are decorative, but the h1/subtitle/tab text are primary UI.

ppt-web is a multi-locale app whose primary audience is Slovak (react-i18next is the standard; sibling registry-adjacent pages such as person-months/pages/PersonMonthsPage.tsx use `t('personMonths.form.year')` etc.). A Slovak/Czech/German manager sees the registry page's header and tabs in English regardless of selected language. This is the same i18n-gap class already filed for other ppt-web pages (dispute-list-no-i18n, moderation-no-i18n, dsa-reports-no-i18n) but on a page not previously flagged for it.

Landable frontend-only remedy: add `useTranslation()` and move the header/subtitle/tab strings into the registry i18n namespace (mirroring PersonMonthsPage). Low severity (+1, i18n gap per the skill's severity table, explicitly not a nit). Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest asserting the translated key renders. Confidence medium: hardcoded strings and the absent i18n import are confirmed by static read; no runtime locale switch was exercised.
